transcript:
Meeting header:
- Date: 2026-01-29
- Time: 16:00 PT
- Duration: 42 min
- Attendees: Jordan Lee (Redwood AE), Priya Nair (Redwood SE), Evan Martinez (Redwood SE), Michael Young (CedarBridge CTO), Sana Rao (Lead ML), Daniel Cho (Infra), Ava Lopez (Product)

Summary:
Jordan: quick porting playbook walkthrough and parity checklist, demo console and Optimize suggestions. Customer wants to move from mix of OpenAI/Anthropic/Together endpoints to single Redwood API with minimum regression in latency and cost.

Topics:
- Parity mapping (API surface, params, function calling)
- Streaming + tool-calling differences
- Embeddings and vector store migration
- Dedicated vs hosted economics + VPC/on-prem constraints
- Security: SOC2, KMS, audit logs
- Pilot plan + benchmarks

Transcript body:
[00:00] Jordan (AE): hey everyone thanks for joining, I'll do a quick agenda, Priya and Evan from SE will jump into the mapping and console demo, michael you said you had some specific SLOs and infra questions so we'll leave time for that, sound good?
[00:14] Michael (CTO): yep that works, thanks. big thing for us is parity — we need behavior close to OpenAI and Anthropic in our user flows, not perfect but no regressions on correctness.
[00:28] Priya (SE): yeah understood. just to confirm, you're currently running a hybrid — OpenAI for chat/generation, Anthropic for safety-sensitive completions, and Together for high-throughput batch scoring?
[00:40] Sana (ML): correct. Together for embeddings and bulk rerank, OpenAI for the chat backend, Anthropic for some internal safety checks. we want consolidate for cost and observability.
[00:53] Evan (SE): cool. we'll show a parity checklist: endpoint mapping, temperature/top-p equivalents, function calling differences, streaming token behavior, and embedding dimension/normalization.
[01:06] Jordan (AE): also we'll highlight where Redwood Optimize suggests quantization or batching to save on tokens and latency tradeoffs.
[01:19] Daniel (Infra): quick infra note — we need VPC peering and customer-managed KMS for keys. private deployment is on the table if dedicated doesn't meet residency rules.
[01:29] Priya (SE): got it. on auth side we support SAML/SSO, RBAC at route level, and the private control plane can integrate with your KMS/HSM. we'll share the SOC2 doc after.
[01:42] Michael: okay good. show us the mapping.

[02:05] Priya (SE): (shares screen) starting with generation: OpenAI 'chat.completions' -> Redwood /v1/chat. the main params map directly, temperature/top_p map 1:1, but a couple of gotchas — OpenAI's stop token handling and streaming deltas differ slightly. Redwood's streaming flushes partial tokens on chunk boundaries which can change timing, but not tokenization. so we recommend keeping stop sequences server-side if you rely on exact token boundaries.
[02:35] Sana: any runtime change to content? like subtle wording shifts?
[02:40] Priya: there can be small differences due to underlying model variants. our parity guide includes prompt adjustments and a short eval harness to catch regression. we'll provide a sample eval set.
[02:55] Evan (SE): for Anthropic-style safety checks — you currently call Anthropic for a safety verdict. on Redwood you can run the same model family or use a dedicated safety route and attach a function-caller shim. we emulate 'constitution' prompts with structured function outputs to preserve your downstream logic. transcription note: sometimes 'constitution' is mis-transcribed as 'constriction' in the logs, sorry.
[03:20] Daniel: about function-calling — does Redwood support the same JSON schema enforcement? we have strict schema validation.
[03:27] Evan: yes, we support structured outputs and schema-enforced function calling. slight difference: we return a function call hint in the streaming envelope earlier, so you can pre-allocate memory. edge case if you rely on exact top-of-stream markers, we'll show sample SDK usage.
[03:45] Jordan: demo time — console and Optimize.
[04:05] Priya: (narrating) console view: model catalog, pinned versions, route configs. here is a mapping example for your chat route — we import your curl call and generate a Redwood route with pinned model, token limits, and a canary policy. link in chat: https://drive.google.com/cedarbridge-parity (placeholder).
[04:35] Sana: can we bulk-import endpoints? We have dozens.
[04:40] Priya: yes, we have an import tool and a migration script. we'll send the gist. also Optimize will flag mismatches — e.g., your Together batch jobs would gain 20-35% cost reduction with our auto-batching + int8 quantization suggestion for that workload.
[05:02] Michael: numbers?
[05:05] Evan: rough ballpark from similar customers: Together batch embedding flows saw unit token cost drop ~24% with auto-batching and prefix cache; latency unchanged or slightly better due to better utilization. for chat endpoints cost per token might drop 10-18% depending on model. we'll run a tailored estimate once we see your token profile.
[05:28] Daniel: what about cold-start latency for occasional big context windows — we need guarantees.
[05:35] Priya: we have SLOs and can propose dedicated reserved capacity for predictable tail latencies. plus prefix caching keeps warm KV for repeated prompts. dedicated offers stricter SLOs and you can set burst capacity.
[05:49] Ava (Product): any migration risk to our features like function-calling + streaming in the weekend cutover?
[05:55] Jordan: typical plan is a staged rollout — canary traffic, shadowing, then cutover. we keep your old endpoints running in parallel for a few days so you can fail back instantly.
[06:09] Michael: ok next, embeddings — Together embeddings are 1536-dim, our vector store expects that size. can you return identical dims and normalization?
[06:20] Evan: we can match dims for supported model families; we also support normalization toggles. we will include an embeddings parity script to verify dot-product behavior against your store.
[06:33] Sana: we use a custom rerank pipeline; small floating diffs changed our top-1 in internal A/B by 2% once — will that be an issue?
[06:41] Priya: that's why we recommend a small validation rollout: run a batch pass on recent queries to compare top-K. Optimize will compute quality regressions and alert. we can keep older model as fallback.
[06:55] Daniel: security checklist? KMS, audit logs, data residency?
[07:01] Priya: we have KMS integrations (customer-managed), full audit logs at token-level, SOC2 Type II and ISO artifacts available. private deployment option supports on-prem and VPC-only control plane.
[07:16] Michael: great. can you share the SOC2 link?
[07:20] Jordan: yes will send after the call (action item).
[07:25] Sana: about tests — do you provide any automated regression harness?
[07:29] Evan: Yes, we have an Eval harness that runs your eval prompts and produces diff reports, with configurable thresholds. we'll run your set and produce a regression report during POC.
[07:40] Jordan: quick pause — does anyone have objections to pilot?
[07:44] Michael: no, but we need infra sign-off for private/dedicated.
[07:48] Daniel: correct. need to verify networking, KMS, and egress rules.
[07:52] Jordan: understood. we'll scope a POC that includes: import endpoints, run regression eval on sample set, 1-week traffic canary, and perf micro-benchmarks.
[08:05] Ava: timeline?
[08:07] Jordan: propose 4–6 week POC: week 1 scoping and infra prep, week 2 import and baseline runs, week 3 canary with partial traffic, week 4 finalize and do cost/quality signoff. we can compress if needed.
[08:22] Michael: sounds good. cost question again — can you show an example hosted vs dedicated estimate?
[08:27] Evan: we'll send a spreadsheet with example numbers — quick rule: dedicated has higher committed cost but predictable unit price; hosted has low start but variable. we'll annotate with your profile once you share usage.
[08:40] Sana: any quirks from Together models? We use some custom tokenization for pre-tokenized inputs.
[08:47] Priya: mention: if you're pre-tokenizing, Redwood supports token-level input but you'll need to align tokenizer versions; we can run tokenization parity check.
[08:58] Jordan: we have about 12 minutes left — demo a short console import flow and show Optimize recommendations.
[09:12] Priya: (screen) import pipeline: paste sample OpenAI request, map to Redwood route, choose model family, pin, set canary percentage. Optimize: shows batch sizing suggestions, suggested quantization (int8) for batch embeddings, and a predicted cost delta. also shows a regression alert that ties to eval set — you can flip on auto-rollback.
[09:45] Michael: that auto-rollback is key. we can't risk degrade in prod.
[09:50] Jordan: yes, automatic fallback to previous model/version and capacity tier.
[09:56] Sana: what about telemetry into our internal observability? we want token-level breadcrumbs in our tracing platform.
[10:02] Evan: we export traces via OpenTelemetry and have a Redwood tracing hook you can pipe into your existing system. we also provide per-request metadata for correlation ids.
[10:15] Daniel: okay, final questions: legal/procurement?
[10:18] Jordan: we'll send procurement checklist and example contract redlines. legal can be looped in after POC scoping.

[10:30] Recap and next steps:
- Jordan: send SOC2/ISO, pricing options, and migration gist.
- Priya: upload parity mapping gist and sample eval harness.
- Evan: perf micro-benchmark plan and Optimize suggested config.
- Daniel: share token profile and monthly volumes (customer).

[10:55] Michael: thanks all. we'll review docs and confirm POC kickoff next week.
[11:03] Jordan: thanks everyone, we'll follow up with calendar invite for scoping session.

Notes and links mentioned:
- placeholder parity spreadsheet: https://bit.ly/rwd-porting-example

End of transcript.
